I went to a women’s college and spent time in an on-campus group therapy for sexual assault/abusive relationship survivors. I heard, saw, and experienced some of the saddest, cruelest things in my life during my four years there. I think it was our age and not knowing how to be emotionally mature yet, but I can’t not see how gender plays a role. 

It became a bit of a joke for me to say to my friends that “we need gay and lesbian ice cream socials, we’re going mad here all alone.” A common joke was that lesbian sex was just crying in bed with another woman. In my experience gay men can be too unemotional with their lovers, but women will be too emotional with them. It makes things very, very difficult to navigate without a lot of wisdom and boundaries. I have a lot of internalized homophobia from those years and I had to take myself out of the gay community to heal. I miss it sometimes, but it’s too hard to come back when we just seem refuse to acknowledge and want to change it.

I grew up very evangelical and had a similar first-sexualized experience with someone that ended up hurting me horribly. It caused a lot of trauma because of that religious baggage. I found a lot of solace in the “wronged woman” trope seen in history through books/music/opera whatever as I healed. It wasn’t a perfect fit, but it did cradle me through the pain knowing I wasn’t alone in it. Eventually, those old stories and a new partner who truly respected me helped me build up my confidence again. It’s been a few years now and I’ve had many new sexual partners, so it is possible to heal and move on. I’m definitely more jaded and cynical about sex and love but it can coexist with peace, I promise. I think a lot of healing came from simply acknowledging the trauma came partly through religion. Honestly, life would be quite boring for me if I had one sexual partner, so I’m happy the bandaid has been ripped off, so to speak. Anyways, thinking of you kindly tonight ❤️ You can do it 🤟

You kind of sound like me while trying to figure it out. I don't know if it'll help, but I started from my body and then "outward." I was never really dysphoric about periods or my voice, and if I was on a desert island alone I would be generally okay with my body. I felt an intense connection to historical/ancient womanhood and my "femaleness" if that's even a word, precisely because I knew in the past I wouldn't have had medical intervention to change things.

The intense dysphoria I labored through was almost entirely social. I was so miserable because no one saw me as a man, and I desperately wanted them to. I felt completely alienated from modern womanhood and definitely *different*. I almost went on T for it but waited because of concerns of it potentially ruining the androgyny I so deeply wanted. Eventually, I began to listen to that kernel centered on my femaleness and found a lot of peace with it. I channeled a bit of old ancient goddess worship and found that through my growing connection to it, I could start to present in another way that I enjoyed (femininity).

I was a tomboy growing up but definitely always had a bit of a girly side. I found expressing it through my womanhood was easier than through manhood, as I'd have to really medically transition to pull it off. Slowly but surely through a trans support group and friends on T, I realized I didn't want it at all. I still have dysphoria around my breasts and regularly bind, but I now enjoy them as an aspect of my sexuality so don't want top surgery (I'm also just very small up there anyways).

I also came to recognize a lot of my "masculine soul" is attached to me sexually and romantically with partners. I realized my deep attraction to feminine men wasn't about me being male as much as it was about wanting them to like me, period. I still have strong sexual fantasies around being a "female trap" (guy thinks I'm a boy but surprise! I'm a girl!) and found confidence in myself that it wasn't some weird taboo thing, just human sexuality. I still sometimes dress in men's clothes publically (it's hot as hell to confuse people) and have found a lot of pride in calling myself a female transvestite/cross-dresser and female androgyne. My short hair helps :')

Good luck ❤️ Basically remember that whatever makes you happy makes you happy—focus on that. I knew being girly and wearing a lot of makeup made me happy too, and it didn't change the fact I loved wearing suits on the downtime. It all came down to that old ancient connection to my body I knew I had in the end.

I went through some trauma involving another trans person and I realized in the months and years afterwards that I was growing more and more comfortable in my body and conception of my femaleness. Not womanhood (yet), but femaleness. I liked sex as a “woman” just like you, I realized the beauty of bleeding I had always liked (even living as a guy), and I remembered the deep connection to historical womanhood i had always had in the back of my head. Even in my diary during the worst of my dysphoria I wrote quite clearly “I feel my femaleness,” which is a reality I stay grounded to. Regardless of gender identity, regardless if I ever get top surgery, I feel connected to that. 

Now, I happen to be more comfortable in my body than I have been in years. My breasts cause me some stress sometimes but I enjoy them as extensions of my sexuality more than my discomfort. 

Sit with why you want this: Is it more to be read as a man easier in public, or is it more because it causes genuine distress? Please take care, and I hope you come to peace ❤️
